{{Short description|Polytope of operations}}
In [[category theory]], a branch of mathematics, an '''opetope''', a portmanteau of "[[operation (algebra)|operation]]" and "[[polytope]]", is a [[shape]] that captures higher-dimensional [[substitution (algebra)|substitution]]s.<ref>{{cite book
| last1=Leinster | first1=Tom | author-link1=Tom Leinster
| chapter=Opetopes
| title=Higher Operads, Higher Categories
| year=2004
| series=London Mathematical Society Lecture Notes Series
| volume=298
| pages=216–260
| publisher=Cambridge University Press
| isbn=0-521-53215-9
| doi=10.1017/CBO9780511525896.010}}</ref> It was introduced by [[John C. Baez]] and James Dolan so that they could define a [[weak n-category|weak ''n''-category]] as a certain [[presheaf (category theory)|presheaf]] on the category of opetopes.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Baez|first1=John C.|last2=Dolan|first2=James|date=1997-02-10|title=Higher-Dimensional Algebra III: n-Categories and the Algebra of Opetopes|journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |volume=135 |issue=2 |pages=145–206|arxiv=q-alg/9702014|bibcode=1997q.alg.....2014B|doi=10.1006/aima.1997.1695|doi-access=free}}</ref>
